note: The loadout slot map. Eight questions with real answers, replacing a flat list of 84 checkboxes. Authored here and joined into the console data (ship/data/ship-data.js) by library/tools/project.py; deliberately NOT a field inside skills.registry.json, which library/tools/project.py regenerates. Every slot has a default, so a loadout is valid untouched. A skill with no slot is not a choice - it is the browsable capability library. `owner` is the console's five-agent display model (Convenium.Design/Athena/Calliope/Hephaestus/Hermes), which no runtime reads. `runtimeOwner` is the agent in library/agents/ that actually holds the slot in both hosts. Verified 2026-09-04 against .codex/agents/ and .claude/agents/: the six library agents are the roster every real run has used, including the Savra_v2 run.

slots.name: Craft
slots.question: What does finished feel like?
slots.why: The one slot that changes the output most. Swapping it produces three genuinely different builds from one brief.

candidates.changes: Fluid, physical motion and interruptible gestures; restraint over ornament.
Component-level polish: the invisible details, states and transitions between them.
Editorial typography and scroll choreography; the loudest of the five.
Hierarchy, accessibility and anti-pattern removal before any expression.
Conventional, familiar patterns; the safest and the least distinctive.

slots.name: Direction
slots.question: How is the concept formed?
slots.why: Decides whether the run arrives at a direction by construction, by taste, or by scoring.

candidates.changes: One direction built from the brief's constraints and defended in writing.
The direction is scored against an explicit rubric before it is committed to.

slots.name: Evidence
slots.question: What grounds the decision?
slots.why: Determines what the director is allowed to call a fact.

candidates.changes: The existing page is the evidence: computed styles, real behaviour, measured defects.
Supplied references are the evidence. The entry point for greenfield work.
People are the evidence. Slowest, and the only one that can contradict the brief.
Measurement is the evidence, and every claim carries an event contract.

slots.name: Structure
slots.question: How is the product organised?
slots.why: Chooses whether the run reasons about information first or about components first.

candidates.changes: Information architecture first: routes, hierarchy and navigation before any screen.
Component inventory first: the library's primitives set what the screens can be.

slots.name: Motion
slots.question: How does it move?
slots.why: Motion is the easiest place to spend a budget with nothing to show. The default is the smallest thing that works.

candidates.changes: State feedback only: tweens, easing, reduced-motion. Nothing scroll-driven.
Adds sequencing, for choreography that has to arrive in an order.
Adds scroll-linked motion, pinning and parallax. The most expensive answer here.
For a React or Next.js target: useGSAP, refs and cleanup on unmount.
A WebGL surface with a non-WebGL fallback. Opt-in, and it must earn its cost.

slots.name: Media
slots.question: Where do assets come from?
slots.why: The slot that decides whether anything is generated at all, and who owns the rights.

candidates.changes: Nothing is produced without an approved manifest. Sourcing before generation.
Generated stills and video, recorded in the manifest with their prompts.
Generated stills only, through the image model already available.
Transform and prepare media that already exists. Generates nothing.

slots.name: Copy
slots.question: Who writes the words?
slots.why: An interface is mostly language, and this is the only slot that owns it.

candidates.changes: New copy written against the positioning: headlines, value propositions, calls to action.
The existing copy is kept and sharpened. Preserves the client's voice.

slots.name: Verify
slots.question: What counts as done?
slots.why: Whatever is chosen here is the only definition of finished the run will honour.

candidates.changes: States, viewports, keyboard, reduced motion and console health, observed not asserted.
Scored against the rubric. Catches a weak concept that passes every check.
Frame cost and jank. Only meaningful when the Motion slot bought something expensive.
